title.sl: Navade: would, be used to, get used to
title.de: Gewohnheiten: would, be used to, get used to
title.it: Le abitudini: would, be used to, get used to
title.en: We would walk; I'm used to it

goal.sl: Poveš, kaj se je ponavljalo (We would walk), in kaj ti je običajno ali postaja (I'm used to it, You'll get used to it), in ločiš to od used to.
goal.de: Du sagst, was früher immer wieder geschah (We would walk) und was für dich normal ist oder wird (I'm used to it, You'll get used to it), und unterscheidest das von used to.
goal.it: Dici che cosa succedeva ogni volta (We would walk) e che cosa per te è normale o lo sta diventando (I'm used to it, You'll get used to it), e lo distingui da used to.
goal.en: You can say what happened again and again (We would walk) and what is or is becoming normal for you (I'm used to it, You'll get used to it), and tell it from used to.

say.sl: **would** + osnovna oblika pove, kaj se je v preteklosti ponavljalo. **When I was a boy, we would walk to school.** (Ko sem bil deček, smo hodili v šolo peš.) **Every Sunday Granny would bake bread.** (Vsako nedeljo je babica pekla kruh.) Kratko **'d**: **We'd walk to school.** Najprej povej, kdaj.
say.de: **would** + Grundform sagt, was früher immer wieder geschah. **When I was a boy, we would walk to school.** (Als ich ein Bub war, gingen wir zu Fuß in die Schule.) **Every Sunday Granny would bake bread.** (Jeden Sonntag backte die Oma Brot.) Kurz **'d**: **We'd walk to school.** Sag zuerst, wann.
say.it: **would** + forma base dice che cosa succedeva ogni volta nel passato. **When I was a boy, we would walk to school.** (Da bambino andavamo a scuola a piedi.) **Every Sunday Granny would bake bread.** (Ogni domenica la nonna faceva il pane.) Breve **'d**: **We'd walk to school.** Prima di' quando.
say.en: **would** + the base form says what happened again and again in the past. **When I was a boy, we would walk to school.** **Every Sunday Granny would bake bread.** Short **'d**: **We'd walk to school.** Say when first.

examples.en: When I was a boy, we would walk to school.
examples.sl: Ko sem bil deček, smo hodili v šolo peš.
examples.de: Als ich ein Bub war, gingen wir zu Fuß in die Schule.
examples.it: Da bambino andavamo a scuola a piedi.

examples.en: Every Sunday Granny would bake bread.
examples.sl: Vsako nedeljo je babica pekla kruh.
examples.de: Jeden Sonntag backte die Oma Brot.
examples.it: Ogni domenica la nonna faceva il pane.

explain.de:

- Every Sunday we would walk to the tarn.
explain.it:
**Allora, ogni volta: would + forma base**

explain.en:
**Again and again then: would + the base form**
- Every Sunday we would walk to the tarn.

say.sl: **would** velja za to, kar si {m:delal|f:delala}, ne za to, kako je bilo. Za stanje **used to**: **We used to have a dog.** (Včasih smo imeli psa.) **He used to live in Leeds.** (Včasih je živel v Leedsu.) Dejanja pa oboje: **We used to walk.** **We would walk.**
say.de: **would** gilt für das, was man tat, nicht dafür, wie es war. Für einen Zustand **used to**: **We used to have a dog.** (Früher hatten wir einen Hund.) **He used to live in Leeds.** (Früher wohnte er in Leeds.) Für Handlungen beides: **We used to walk.** **We would walk.**
say.it: **would** vale per ciò che si faceva, non per com'era. Per uno stato **used to**: **We used to have a dog.** (Una volta avevamo un cane.) **He used to live in Leeds.** (Una volta abitava a Leeds.) Per le azioni tutti e due: **We used to walk.** **We would walk.**
say.en: **would** is for what you did, not for how things were. For how things were, **used to**: **We used to have a dog.** (not *We would have a dog*) **He used to live in Leeds.** For what you did, either: **We used to walk.** **We would walk.**

examples.en: We used to have a dog.
He used to live in Leeds.

rows: We used to have a dog.

say.sl: **be used to** + -ing ali samostalnik pomeni, da ti je nekaj običajno. **I'm used to getting up early.** (Navajen{m:|f:a} sem zgodaj vstajati.) **She's used to the rain.** (Navajena je dežja.) Zanikano **I'm not used to it**, vprašanje **Are you used to it?** Slovenščina ima tu nedoločnik, angleščina -ing.
say.de: **be used to** + -ing oder ein Nomen heißt, dass etwas für dich normal ist. **I'm used to getting up early.** (Ich bin es gewohnt, früh aufzustehen.) **She's used to the rain.** (Sie ist den Regen gewohnt.) Verneint **I'm not used to it**, die Frage **Are you used to it?** Deutsch hat hier den Infinitiv, Englisch -ing.
say.it: **be used to** + -ing o un nome vuol dire che per te una cosa è normale. **I'm used to getting up early.** (Sono abituat{m:o|f:a} ad alzarmi presto.) **She's used to the rain.** (È abituata alla pioggia.) Al negativo **I'm not used to it**, la domanda **Are you used to it?** L'italiano qui ha l'infinito, l'inglese -ing.
say.en: **be used to** + -ing or a noun means something is normal for you. **I'm used to getting up early.** (not *I'm used to get up early*) **She's used to the rain.** With not **I'm not used to it**, to ask **Are you used to it?**

examples.en: I'm used to getting up early.
examples.de: Ich bin es gewohnt, früh aufzustehen.

rows: I'm used to getting up early.

say.sl: **get used to** pomeni, da to postaja običajno: **You'll get used to it.** (Navadil{m:|f:a} se boš.) **I'm getting used to the rain.** (Počasi se navajam na dež.) **She got used to driving on the left.** (Navadila se je voziti po levi.)
say.de: **get used to** heißt, dass es normal wird: **You'll get used to it.** (Du wirst dich daran gewöhnen.) **I'm getting used to the rain.** (Ich gewöhne mich langsam an den Regen.) **She got used to driving on the left.** (Sie gewöhnte sich daran, links zu fahren.)
say.it: **get used to** vuol dire che lo sta diventando: **You'll get used to it.** (Ti ci abituerai.) **I'm getting used to the rain.** (Mi sto abituando alla pioggia.) **She got used to driving on the left.** (Si è abituata a guidare a sinistra.)
say.en: **get used to** means it's becoming normal: **You'll get used to it.** **I'm getting used to the rain.** **She got used to driving on the left.** (not *She got used to drive on the left*)

say.sl: **to** je tu mali predlog pred -ing, kot v **look forward to**: **I'm used to it.** Sliši se kot *use to*, zato ljudje pišejo tudi *I'm use to it*. Pisno velja **I'm used to it**. Za njim je -ing, ne osnovna oblika: **used to getting up**.
say.de: **to** ist hier das kleine Wort vor -ing, wie in **look forward to**: **I'm used to it.** Es klingt wie *use to*, darum schreibt man auch *I'm use to it*. Geschrieben gilt **I'm used to it**. Danach -ing, nicht die Grundform: **used to getting up**.
say.it: **to** qui è la parolina prima di -ing, come in **look forward to**: **I'm used to it.** Suona come *use to*, perciò si scrive anche *I'm use to it*. Per iscritto vale **I'm used to it**. Dopo viene -ing, non la forma base: **used to getting up**.
say.en: **to** here is the small word before -ing, as in **look forward to**: **I'm used to it.** It sounds like *use to*, so people also write *I'm use to it*. Writing wants **I'm used to it**. After it comes -ing, not the base form: **used to getting up**.

examples.de: Ich freue mich darauf, dich zu sehen.

exercises.title: Mrs Hartley's first year
exercises.text: When I came here from Leeds, I wasn't used to ___ (walk) so far. In Leeds I ___ (take) the bus everywhere. I ___ (not know) anyone here at first. In the evenings I would ___ (sit) alone and read. The children ___ (laugh) at my shoes. It took me a year to get used to ___ (be) wet all the time. Now I'm used to ___ (get) up in the dark, and I ___ (not mind) the rain at all.

translation.sl: Ko sem prišla sem iz Leedsa, nisem bila navajena toliko hoditi. V Leedsu sem povsod hodila z avtobusom. Sprva tu nisem poznala nikogar. Zvečer sem sedela sama in brala. Otroci so se smejali mojim čevljem. Leto dni sem potrebovala, da sem se navadila, da sem ves čas mokra. Zdaj sem navajena vstajati v temi in dež me sploh ne moti.
translation.de: Als ich aus Leeds hierherkam, war ich es nicht gewohnt, so weit zu gehen. In Leeds nahm ich überall den Bus. Anfangs kannte ich hier niemanden. Am Abend saß ich allein da und las. Die Kinder lachten über meine Schuhe. Ich brauchte ein Jahr, um mich daran zu gewöhnen, dauernd nass zu sein. Jetzt bin ich es gewohnt, im Dunkeln aufzustehen, und der Regen stört mich gar nicht.
translation.it: Quando sono arrivata qui da Leeds, non ero abituata a camminare tanto. A Leeds prendevo l'autobus dappertutto. All'inizio qui non conoscevo nessuno. La sera stavo seduta da sola a leggere. I bambini ridevano delle mie scarpe. Mi ci è voluto un anno per abituarmi a essere sempre bagnata. Adesso sono abituata ad alzarmi al buio, e la pioggia non mi dà nessun fastidio.
translation.en: When I came here from Leeds, I wasn't used to walking so far. In Leeds I used to take the bus everywhere. I didn't know anyone here at first. In the evenings I would sit alone and read. The children used to laugh at my shoes. It took me a year to get used to being wet all the time. Now I'm used to getting up in the dark, and I don't mind the rain at all.

translation.en: When I was a boy, we used to get up at five. My father would wake me with a cup of tea. We had a cow then. I was used to working before school. Now I can't get used to sleeping so late!
